arguments.chapterText:
Practice hours get quoted as if they were the whole story. In the study, though, the hours alone did not separate the strongest students from the rest. The difference lay in how each session was planned.

Sourdough starters need feeding every twelve hours, or they sour and lose their rise. A baker who skips a feeding loses a whole day of work.

Teachers who set each task in advance gave their students a clear target for every session. The students who worked toward those targets improved fastest.
arguments.coreIdea: Expertise grows from planned practice, not from the hours alone.
